strings.opt_hint_panelcss:
This CSS is injected into the panel own shadow root. The panel is not in the page DOM, so putting it into Stylus / user.css will not work - write it here.
Available hooks: #rt-panel (the panel itself; its id selector outranks the presets, so you usually do not need !important), [data-rt-theme="dark"] and [data-rt-theme="light"] (per-theme rules), .rt-head .rt-cfg .rt-lang .rt-out .rt-src .rt-slot .rt-slot-h .rt-slot-name .rt-slot-b .rt-acts .rt-act .rt-foot .rt-msg .rt-more .rt-diag .d-k .d-v .rt-btn .rt-dot. These names will not change (if they ever do, aliases will be provided).
strings.opt_hint_trigidle: How long the button stays after you stop moving the mouse. Hovering pauses the countdown.
strings.opt_hint_trigleave: How long it stays after the pointer leaves the button, so it does not vanish while you are on your way to click it.
strings.opt_hint_trigstyle: The little button that appears next to the selection. This only affects the button itself. Globe is a line icon whose colour follows the theme.
strings.opt_hint_trigsvg: Paste a whole <svg>…</svg> block. Pasted in as-is but must pass the guards: no script, no external links, no event attributes.
strings.opt_hint_uilang: Only affects the interface language, not the translation target. Language packs are about 10–40 KB, fetched from GitHub and not bundled; if the download fails the current language stays.
strings.opt_hint_vars: Values defined here can be referenced in request templates as {{name}} — e.g. put the API key in {{apiKey}} instead of typing it into the template.
strings.opt_hist_empty: No records yet (or the count above is 0).
strings.opt_img_badge: Has an image request template, so screenshots use it in direct-image mode
strings.opt_imgtpl_hint:
Fill this in (on the main request or any fallback) for this config to appear in the OCR tab image config list. It handles images; the template above still handles selected text, and leaving it empty falls back to that template.
Write it like a multimodal request, e.g. {"role":"user","content":[{"type":"image_url","image_url":{"url":"{{image}}"}},{"type":"text","text":"Translate the text in this image to {{target}}, output only the translation"}]}
Here {{text}} is empty - in direct mode the image itself is the source.
strings.opt_imgtpl_ph: Empty = images reuse the template above
strings.opt_imgtpl_sep: ====== image request template (used for direct image passing) ======
strings.opt_imgtpl_title: Image request template (optional, click to fill)
strings.opt_lang_samehint: The panel header has one too and both share the same value, so you do not have to come back here just to switch language for a moment.

strings.opt_set_106: The backup copy contains your API keys in plain text; send it only to yourself. Ticking “encrypted export” protects it with a passphrase (AES-GCM) — the passphrase is not recoverable, so losing it means losing the file.
strings.opt_set_109: Automatically blanks the values of variables whose name contains “key” so the recipient can put in their own. Keys typed directly into a request template are not detected, so check before sharing.
strings.opt_set_112: Replaces the current configs, variables, settings and OCR wholesale. Encrypted files ask for the passphrase first.
strings.opt_set_120: Keep the existing configs (checked ones are appended, same names overwritten); unchecked = replace everything

strings.opt_tpl_hint_ocr: Sent byte-for-byte apart from placeholder substitution; write the prompt into the request text, not into a placeholder. The three image placeholders differ - see the tag tooltips above. Form APIs such as Baidu need {{imageUrlEncoded}} (a + in base64 that is not turned into %2B is read as a space). Put the key in {{apiKey}} instead of hard-coding it.
strings.opt_tpl_hint_text: Either a curl command or a raw HTTP message; sent byte-for-byte apart from placeholder substitution. JSON must not contain literal newlines (write \n), escape double quotes as \"; a leading # starts a comment.

strings.bing_page_failed: Could not load the Bing translator page: HTTP $1$
strings.bing_parse_failed: Could not parse the auth parameters from bing.com/translator (Bing may have changed)
strings.bing_token_expired: Bing token expired; re-fetched and retried
strings.bing_empty: Bing returned an empty response. Usually the token expired or you were rate-limited — one retry is normally enough. If it is always empty, the request is probably going through a proxy whose node blocks this endpoint; add a direct rule for bing.com in your proxy client (DOMAIN-SUFFIX,bing.com,DIRECT).
strings.bing_not_json: Bing returned something that is not JSON: $1$
strings.parse_no_url: No URL parsed — make sure the request contains a full https:// address
strings.parse_get_body: A GET request has a body; the browser will drop it
strings.parse_at_file: The body is @file — curl would read a local file, which an extension cannot do, so this @… is sent as the body
strings.parse_upload: -F / --form / -T need local files, which an extension does not support; this part was ignored
strings.parse_urlencode: --data-urlencode values are not URL-encoded (curl would encode them; here they are sent as-is) — encode them yourself in the template if needed
strings.err_send_failed: Request failed: $1$ (check the URL, whether a proxy is blocking it, or whether the site allows extension access)
strings.err_no_extract: Request succeeded but no translation was extracted. Structure: $1$
